election_dates.primarySnippet: § 8-100. Elections; dates of and hours for voting. 1. (a) A primary election shall be held on the fourth Tuesday in June before every general election unless otherwise changed by an act of the legislature.
election_dates.generalSnippet: (c) The general election shall be held annually on the Tuesday next succeeding the first Monday in November.

state_background_check.value: No — New York removes a sitting officeholder convicted of a felony (or of a crime violating their oath of office) from an office they already hold, but no provision found bars someone from becoming a candidate for office in the first place; and the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state regardless
state_background_check.snippet: § 30. Creation of vacancies. 1. Every office shall be vacant upon the happening of one of the following events before the expiration of the term thereof: ... e. His or her conviction of a felony, conviction of a crime involving a violation of his or her oath of office, or upon entering a guilty plea in federal court to a felony, or upon entering a guilty plea in federal court to a crime involving a violation of his or her oath of office. Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

platform.value: Unapologetically backs the blue, strongly opposes cashless bail policies and any effort to defund the police, and will fight to get law enforcement the funding, training, and tools they need.
platform.snippet: Kailee Buller unapologetically backs the blue. As the daughter of an Auburn corrections officer, she knows the sacrifices law enforcement families make and the risks officers face every time they put on the uniform. She believes Central New Yorkers deserve safe communities and a justice system that prioritizes victims – not criminals. Kailee strongly opposes cashless bail policies and any effort to defund the police. She will fight to get law enforcement the funding, training, and tools they need to do their jobs effectively and keep our community safe.

platform.value: Supports investing in outcomes so schools are rewarded for results, expanding vocational training and trade schools, making college more affordable through greater transparency and accountability, curriculum transparency for parents, and expansion of Pell Grants for workforce training programs.
platform.snippet: Investing in outcomes – so schools are rewarding for results, not just spending. Expanding Vocational Training and Trade Schools which champion apprenticeships and career training that connects students directly to the good-paying jobs being created right here. Making college more affordable through greater transparency on college costs, accountability for outcomes, and realistic repayment options — without sticking taxpayers with the bill. Curriculum transparency for parents while ensuring teachers have the resources they need to do their jobs well. Expansion of Pell Grants for Workforce Training because financial aid shouldn t be limited to four-year degrees and be opened to vocational and workforce programs too.

platform.value: Believes these commitments must be honored, full stop, and will work to strengthen program integrity so that every dollar goes to the people who earned it.
platform.snippet: Social Security and Medicare are promises made to the American people. Central New York seniors have spent their entire working lives paying into these programs — and they have earned every dollar of those benefits. Kailee Buller believes these commitments must be honored, full stop. She will also work to strengthen program integrity so that every dollar of Social Security and Medicare goes to the people who earned it — not to bad actors gaming the system.

bio_summary.value: Kailee Buller is an Auburn native, food and economic policy advocate, and working mom who has spent her career fighting to lower costs, expand access to real food, and create opportunity for working families and farmers. She served as Chief of Staff at the U.S. Department of Agriculture and has held other senior leadership roles within the federal government and national policy organizations. In those roles, she worked to cut red tape, strengthen American agriculture, support small businesses, and protect jobs across the food and energy supply chain.
